schemes.scheme_name: PDS / One Nation One Ration Card
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS)

eligibility.criterion: Must be an existing NFSA ration card holder (AAY or PHH category)
Aadhaar number must be linked (seeded) with the ration card
Any NFSA beneficiary can use ONORC in any of 36 states — no new card needed
Families identified in SECC 2011 data — rural deprivation OR urban occupational categories
Urban workers in 11 occupational categories including construction, domestic, street vendor, transport, security guard, washer, tailor
All senior citizens aged 70+ are eligible regardless of income
Any unorganised worker aged 16-59 years who is NOT in EPFO or ESIC
For OSH Code protection: any worker who migrated from one state to another for work
Must be a construction worker aged 18-60 with at least 90 days of construction work in last 12 months
Interstate migrant construction workers are eligible — register with the BOCW Board of the STATE WHERE YOU ARE CURRENTLY WORKING
Any adult member (18 years or above) of a rural household, willing to do unskilled manual work.
Applicant must reside in a rural area (urban households are not covered).
Household must register with the local Gram Panchayat and obtain a Job Card before demanding work.

beneficiary_categories.description: Poorest of the poor — entitled to 35 kg of free food grain per household per month
NFSA beneficiary households — entitled to 5 kg of free food grain per person per month
NFSA cardholders who have migrated to another state for work — can use ration at any FPS with Aadhaar authentication
Rural households with at least one of 7 deprivation criteria — no adult 16-59, SC/ST, landless labourers, disabled members, no shelter
Construction workers, domestic workers, street vendors, transport workers, security guards, sweepers, tailors, electricians in urban areas
All citizens aged 70 and above regardless of income — get additional Rs 5 lakh top-up cover
Largest category of migrant workers — masons, carpenters, plumbers, painters, labourers
Maids, cooks, babysitters, security guards working in private households
All workers at building construction sites — masons, carpenters, plumbers, welders, painters, labourers, helpers
Any household residing in rural areas whose adult members are willing to do unskilled manual work.
One-third of MGNREGA beneficiaries are required to be women; the scheme actively prioritises women's participation.
The scheme specifically encourages participation of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe households.

benefits.description: Free food grains (rice, wheat) from any Fair Price Shop in any state — 5 kg per person/month (PHH) or 35 kg per household/month (AAY). Free since January 2023.
Same ration card works in all 36 states and UTs — no new card needed when migrating
Worker can collect part of ration at destination city. Family at home can collect remaining balance at home FPS.

benefits.benefit_name: Rs 5 lakh health insurance per family per year
benefits.description: Rs 5,00,000 per family per year for hospital treatment — covers surgery, medicine, pre and post hospitalisation
No cash payment needed at any empanelled public or private hospital. Show Aadhaar, get treatment.

benefits.benefit_name: Pre-existing conditions covered from day one
benefits.description: All existing medical conditions are covered from the first day — no waiting period
More than 1,900 medical procedures including surgeries, dialysis, cancer treatment, heart surgery, bone operations

benefits.benefit_name: Rs 2 lakh accident insurance via PMSBY
benefits.description: Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or permanent total disability. Rs 1 lakh for partial disability. Auto-linked when you register on e-Shram.
12-digit Universal Account Number card valid across all states. Single identity for accessing 50+ government schemes.
Under OSH Code 2020, contractor must pay migrant workers at least the minimum wage of the destination state — same as local workers. No wage discrimination allowed.
Contractor must pay displacement allowance — 50% of monthly wages or Rs 75 whichever is higher — when recruiting a migrant worker from their home state.
benefits.amount: 50% of monthly wages or Rs 75 (whichever higher)

benefits.description: Contractor-recruited migrants are entitled to free travel from home to worksite and back after the work period ends.
BOCW Board pays Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh (varies by state) as lump sum to nominee in case of accidental death at construction site. Partial disability gets proportional amount.
Annual scholarship for children of registered BOCW workers from Class 1 to professional courses. Amount varies by state — up to Rs 25,000/year for professional courses.
One-time financial assistance for marriage of registered worker's daughter — Rs 25,000 to Rs 55,000 depending on state.
Monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 3,000 after age 60 for workers who were registered with BOCW Board during their working years.
Financial assistance for hospitalisation of worker and immediate family. Amount varies by state.
Legal guarantee of at least 100 days of wage employment per household per financial year (125 days under VB-G RAM G from July 2026).

If work is not provided within 15 days of a written application, the applicant is entitled to an unemployment allowance from the State Government - at least one-fourth the wage rate for the first 30 days, one-half thereafter.
Wages paid directly to the worker's Aadhaar-linked bank/post office account by Direct Benefit Transfer. Minimum interim base wage Rs 300/day from July 2026 under VB-G RAM G.

documents.description: For biometric authentication at ePoS device at Fair Price Shop
Existing NFSA ration card issued by home state government
Primary identity document for eligibility verification at hospital
Health card issued under PM-JAY — can be generated at any empanelled hospital on the spot using Aadhaar
Mandatory for OTP-based registration on e-Shram portal
Mobile number registered with Aadhaar to receive OTP for e-Shram registration
Bank account number and IFSC code for direct benefit transfer of insurance claims
Primary identity document for BOCW registration
Certificate from contractor or supervisor confirming at least 90 days of construction work in last 12 months. Self-declaration accepted in some states if contractor refuses.
Bank account for direct transfer of BOCW welfare benefits
2-4 recent passport photographs as required by the state BOCW board
Aadhaar of the family head and all adult members - mandatory for identity verification and DBT wage payment.
Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account passbook, needed so wages can be paid directly via DBT.
Ration card, voter ID, or electricity bill establishing rural residence.

application_steps.instruction: Check if your Aadhaar is linked to your ration card. If not, visit any CSC or Food & Civil Supplies office — it is free.
Go to any ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shop (FPS) in the state you are in. Show your Aadhaar number or ration card number.
Give your fingerprint on the ePoS biometric device at the shop. Upon successful authentication, collect your free food grains.
Go to any empanelled government or private hospital. Look for the Ayushman Mitra desk at the hospital entrance or billing counter.
Show your Aadhaar card to the Ayushman Mitra. They will verify your eligibility in the PM-JAY database and generate your Ayushman Card if you don't already have one.
After eligibility is verified, get admitted for cashless treatment. No money needs to be paid upfront. The hospital claims directly from the government.
Go to the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with your Aadhaar card and bank passbook. Registration on e-Shram is completely FREE.
The CSC operator will register you on the e-Shram portal. You will receive a 12-digit UAN (Universal Account Number) and an e-Shram card.
For wage theft or rights violations, go to the nearest District Labour Office (Shram Suvidha Kendra) with your e-Shram UAN card and file a complaint. The contractor can have their licence cancelled.
Get a 90-day work certificate from your contractor or site supervisor. If contractor refuses, use a self-declaration form or get a certificate from a labour NGO.
Visit the nearest CSC or District Labour Office with Aadhaar, work certificate, bank passbook, and 2 passport photos. Fill BOCW Form IV. Pay Rs 25-50 registration fee (free in some states).
Register with the BOCW Board of the STATE WHERE YOU ARE CURRENTLY WORKING — not your home state. You can register in both states.
Visit your local Gram Panchayat office and request a Job Card application form (free of cost), or apply on plain paper.
Submit names, ages, and Aadhaar details of all adult household members willing to do unskilled manual work; Job Card is issued within 15 days after verification.
To demand work: submit a written application to the Gram Panchayat specifying when and for how long you need work (minimum 14 days continuous).
Register and apply for a Job Card via the UMANG mobile app (search 'MGNREGA').

exceptions_and_limitations.description: ONORC portability only works if Aadhaar is seeded (linked) with the ration card. Without Aadhaar linking, inter-state access is not possible.
Only ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shops can process ONORC transactions. Rural shops without ePoS machines cannot offer portability.
Biometric failure (worn fingerprints of manual labourers) can prevent access. In such cases, ask the FPS operator for iris scan option or visit another FPS.
Only empanelled hospitals provide cashless PM-JAY treatment. Non-empanelled hospitals cannot offer this benefit even if they claim to.
OPD (outpatient) expenses are NOT covered under PM-JAY. Only hospitalisation (admission of at least 24 hours) is covered.
Workers already in EPFO or ESIC (formal sector employees) CANNOT register on e-Shram.
OSH Code 2020 protections are stronger for contractor-recruited workers. Self-migrated workers have fewer contractor-specific rights (like transport and displacement allowance).
BOCW card expires if not renewed annually. Claims cannot be made on expired cards. Renew by showing continued construction work (90 days) each year.
BOCW benefit amounts vary significantly by state. Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra have better benefits than some other states. Always check your destination state's BOCW portal for exact amounts.
Urban areas are not covered under MGNREGA - only rural households are eligible.
Only unskilled manual work is guaranteed; skilled or semi-skilled employment is not covered.
The guarantee is capped at 100 days per household per financial year (125 days under VB-G RAM G from July 2026) - additional days are not guaranteed.

official_contacts.description: ONORC national toll-free helpline for ration card portability queries
PM-JAY national helpline for eligibility check, hospital help, and grievances
e-Shram helpline for registration queries and UAN card issues
Ministry of Labour helpline for OSH Code, wage theft, BOCW complaints
CPGRAMS — central grievance portal for all government scheme complaints
Official MGNREGA MIS portal for Job Card details, work status, and payment status.
CPGRAMS centralized public grievance portal for filing MGNREGA complaints.

state_rules.special_rule: Maharashtra has one of the best BOCW benefit packages in India. Self-employed construction workers also eligible.
Tamil Nadu BOCW board provides education scholarships up to Class 12. Registration possible at District Labour Office or CSC.
Gujarat BOCW board — strong accident insurance. Self-declaration accepted for 90-day proof in Gujarat.
Karnataka BOCW provides housing loan assistance in addition to standard benefits.
UP BOCW — major source state. Workers from UP working in other states should register in DESTINATION state, not UP.
ONORC is implemented in all 36 states and UTs. State-specific helplines vary — call 14445 for the nearest FPS.
As of July 2026, ALL 36 states and UTs are covered under PM-JAY including West Bengal. Full pan-India cashless treatment.
Bihar is a major source state. Migrant workers from Bihar should register BOCW in their DESTINATION state, not Bihar.
Telangana BOCW includes skill development training as additional benefit.
Wage rates and helpline numbers vary by state and are notified annually - MGNREGA does not have inter-state portability like ONORC; work is tied to the registered Gram Panchayat.

important_definitions.definition: One Nation One Ration Card — the scheme that makes your ration card valid anywhere in India
Electronic Point of Sale — the machine at the Fair Price Shop where you give your fingerprint to get ration
A helper at every empanelled hospital who assists PM-JAY patients with verification, card creation, and admission — find them at the hospital entrance
Universal Account Number — the 12-digit unique number you get when you register on e-Shram. Valid across all of India.
Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 — the law that gives migrant workers the right to equal wages, safety, and free travel in any state they work in
District Labour Office — the government office where you file complaints against contractors for wage theft or rights violations
A 1% tax on construction projects that funds the state BOCW Welfare Boards — this is why the government has money to give you benefits
The primary document issued to registered households under MGNREGA, needed to demand work; valid for five years.
The Gram Panchayat-level official responsible for day-to-day MGNREGA implementation - registration, verification, and muster roll maintenance.

Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 - the successor legislation to MGNREGA effective July 1, 2026, expanding the guarantee to 125 days with a Rs 300/day minimum wage.
